News.title: Trump vows to avenge deaths of US soldiers ‘many times over’ as furious president blitzes Iran for 10th night
News.content:
DONALD Trump has vowed to enact revenge on Iran “many times over” following the deaths of three US soldiers over the weekend.

It comes as the US president launched fresh strikes across the country for the 10th night running – before Tehran hit back with its own retaliatory attacks.



Washington’s latest blitz was unleashed to “further degrade” Tehran’s ability to attack commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz.

US Central Command (Centcom) said its latest assault hit Iranian “military command centres, maritime capabilities, missile and drone launch sites, and air defense systems”.



In response to the overnight attack, Iran claimed it struck US military targets in Bahrain and Kuwait, as well as two oil tankers in the key waterway, according to state media.

It comes after the White House confirmed the identities of three dead US personnel.

Pte Isabella Gonzales, 19, from Texas, and Lt Tyler James Feehan, 25, from Hawaii were killed in an Iranian blitz on the Muwaffaq Salti base in Jordan over the weekend.

A third soldier went missing in action during the attack.



Unidentified remains have since been found in the area.

The third US soldier died in Iraq on Saturday during a “controlled detonation” of an Iranian drone.

Trump said on Monday following the tragic announcement: “Every time Iran kills an American Soldier they will pay for that killing many times over!”



He said this directive had been passed to Secretary of War, Pete Hegseth, Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, Daniel Caine, and “every Leader in the Military”.

At least 17 US personnel have now been killed in the Iran war since its start on February 28.

Despite tit-for-tat strikes seemingly leaving any peace deal further from reality each day, mediators are reportedly working to help pass through a new one.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran was now locked in a “full-scale war” with the US.

But negotiators are understood to have passed Iran a proposal that would offer a new 10-day ceasefire.



On Monday, Iran’s interior minister landed in Pakistan for two days of talks with the country’s prime minister.

Meanwhile, chaos in the Strait of Hormuz has continued, with the Houthi rebels – an Iran-backed proxy – vowing to establish its own naval blockade against Saudi Arabia.

The terror group claim the move is a response to Saudi strikes on a Houthi-controlled airport in Yemen’s capital last week.

In a chilling sign the conflict may be set to escalate, extra F-16 and F-35 fighter jets from European bases, as well as more aerial refuelling tankers, have been deployed to the region.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

As the now-collapsed peace deal was crumbling last week, Trump received a briefing from ­military chiefs on options to intensify the war.



They included capturing Kharg Island, where 90 per cent of Iran’s oil exports pass through, or bombing Iranian nuclear facilities at Pickaxe Mountain.

News.title: Andy Burnham scraps VAT on electricity bills from October in £850million move funded by axing Keir’s digital ID scheme
News.content:
ANDY Burnham will slash taxes on electricity bills from October to help households in the cost of living crisis.

He has pledged to take VAT off electricity bills which is expected to take £45 off the annual price cap from the autumn.



Energy bills could see another jump later in the year in the wake of the Middle East conflict.

The VAT cut will see it cut on electricity bills from 5 per cent to 0 per cent.



The new Prime Minister vowed to give the public “breathing space” as they battle higher bills and help bring down inflation.

The move comes on top of the £150 reduction brought in at the last Budget.

The policy will cost £850 million in 2026/27 and will be paid for by cancelling the Digital ID cards scheme, which would have cost £1.8 billion.

Mr Burnham said: “Westminster has not been working for people for too long, with families struggling with the cost of living.

“That needs to change. I said I wanted to give people breathing space, and that’s what I’m announcing on my second day as Prime Minister.

“We’re taking immediate action to cut taxes on energy bills, put more money in people’s pockets and bring back hope.”



Other policies that are being weighed up include cutting bus fares and rent controls. A longer term measure could be to raise the tax free personal allowance that has been frozen at £12,570 for five years.

Number 10 said any further action which will include longer-term measures will be taken at the Budget later this year.

Energy firms are expected to pass on the VAT cut to consumers.

Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey MP said: “For too long, too many people have struggled with the cost of living.



'Convincing the public will take more than just warm words' Analysis by Ryan Sabey, Deputy Political Editor ANDY Burnham isn’t wasting any time showing the British people he is on their side as they battle the cost-of-living.

The new Prime Minister was quick out of the blocks outside Downing Street to offer the public some “breathing space” as they grapple with rising bills.

He has been accused of being all about ‘vibes’ but there may be finally be a bit of meat on the bones when it comes to policy.

Speculation has been rife that there may be help coming on bus fares, energy bills and also a change in tax rules to give people a bit more cash in their pockets.

The move is in sheer contrast to when Sir Keir Starmer came to office just over two years ago.

Within weeks, the out-going PM told millions of pensioners that they were going to lose out on their winter fuel payments.

Mr Burnham used his showcase moment – minutes after leaving Buckingham Palace to meet the King – wants to show that he is on their side as he says he will give the people “his all”.

Voters will only have to wait 24 hours until he offers some help and explains how it will be paid for.

It was the first time for many years that an incoming Prime Minister delivered his speech without notes in front of dozens of supporters.

Close aides and the Labour faithful created a party atmosphere in the country’s most famous streets.

But convincing the public out in the country and driving up their living standards will take more than just warm words.

He was at pains to point out to the British people when they say politicians haven’t been on their side.

The PM will offer a “circuit breaker” to what has come before with more power devolved to the regions.

But anyone thinking that a big, bold radical plan for the country will be enacted today they must think again.

A ten-year plan for the country won’t come until later this year. Time will only tell how much of that decade Mr Burnham will preside over.

The true test will be whether feel better off in their pockets and time is short. The clock is already ticking.

“Today’s energy tax cut will give families some breathing room on bills, and provide some reassurance this winter.

“This measure is funded this year from cancelling the Digital ID programme, and it will help bring down inflation while supporting households in every postcode.”

The reduction will be extended to small businesses who qualify for domestic energy alongside eligible charities and residential care homes.

This comes after Mr Burnham’s first speech yesterday in which he promised to “give people some breathing space now”.

His first pledge as prime minister was to end rough sleeping in England using similar schemes to ones he rolled out in Manchester.



Mr Burnham said he will set out his 10 year plan later this year and vowed to be a “circuit-breaker” for Britain.

This began with a bloodbath in the cabinet which saw many ministers loyal to Sir Keir Starmer purged.

In a big surprise Mr Healey was appointed as chancellor yesterday while Rachel Reeves was sacked.

Eco-crusading Ed Miliband had been gunning for the Treasury job — but was instead packed off abroad as Foreign Secretary.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Shabana Mahmood remained as Home Secretary to ­continue pushing through her immigration reforms.



Other casualties included David Lammy, Lord Hermer, Peter Kyle, Steve Reed, Liz Kendall, Nick Thomas-Symonds, Darren Jones, Jo ­Stevens and Hilary Benn.

News.title: El Chapo’s bloodthirsty cartel kingpin pal El Mayo gets life behind bars & will give up £11.2bn in drug profits
News.content:
A RUTHLESS cartel kingpin who reportedly skinned his victims and betrayed former pal El Chapo has been jailed for life.

Mexican druglord Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada spent four decades flooding the US with deadly drugs like heroin, cocaine and fentanyl and ordering gangsters to kill and torture anyone who stood in his way.



He ruled Mexico‘s most powerful drug trafficking syndicate – the Sinaloa Cartel – which he co-founded with notorious gangster Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán in the 1980s.

The kingpin had evaded arrest for decades – despite having a $15million bounty on his head.



The bloodthirsty criminal mastermind was captured in 2024 after El Chapo’s son tricked him into flying to Santa Teresa International Jetport in Texas – where he was met with law enforcement.

He entered a plea deal to spare himself from the death penalty last year – but in exchange will be forced to give up £11.2billion worth of drug profits.

Seven years ago his pal and cartel co-founder Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán was sentenced to life imprisonment after El Mayo told his incarcerated son to hand him in.

Now the same fate awaits Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada.

Speaking to Brooklyn Federal Court on July 20, the notorious cartel boss said he was sorry “for the harm I caused and for the example I set”.

He added, through a translator: “If there’s one thing I can say that has value today, it’s this: the violence must end.



“In Mexico and elsewhere affected by this type of crime, too many lives are lost, too many families are destroyed, and too many young people are trapped in a cycle that leads only to prison or death.”

His friend Guzmán was the flamboyant showman of the crime syndicate – while Zambada was the scheming strategist behind the vile network.

A suspected member of the cartel, Eladio, described his boss El Mayo as “more poisonous than a snake”.



The drug-dealing fiend plead guilty in August 2025 after prosecutors promised not to seek the death penalty.

Prosecutors said Zambada had been “one of the most – if not the most – prolific and powerful narcotraffickers in the world.

“It would be difficult to overstate the magnitude of his crimes and the scale of the corruption, violence, and other harm he spread throughout Mexico, the United States, and the world.”

Nearly half a million people died of fentanyl poisoning in the US last year, according to the government’s accountability office.

The cartel kingpin apologised “to everyone who has suffered or been affected by my actions” and admitted to transporting at least 1.5million kilograms of cocaine – most of which entered the United States.



The 76-year-old will now spend his life in a prison hospital because he suffers from a cocktail of “complex age-related health issues”, said his defence lawyer Frank Perez.

U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of New York Joseph Nocella, Jr. said: “Ismael Zambada Garcia spent nearly four decades poisoning American communities to make billions of dollars in profit and ordering the murders of anyone who stood in his way. Today, that chapter closes for good.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Though El Mayo will now rot behind bars, the deadly cartel he spawned with his associate El Chapo will continue, according to experts who spoke to CNN.

One suggested that the kingpin’s son Ismael “el Mayito Flaco” Zambada Sicairos may be crowned the new leader.

News.title: Granddad flung into air by 1-tonne bison speaks from hospital bed as x-rays show femur broken in 4 places
News.content:
A GRANDAD who was tossed like a rag doll by a bison in Yellowstone and had his bones shattered in multiple pieces has spoken out from his hospital bed.

Carl Isom-McDaniel, 65, was flung 8ft into the air by the animal – weighing one tonne – during a walk with his grandson at the National Park.



Footage shows the beast becoming agitated and charging at the man at full-speed, chasing him through the trees before it eventually hooked him with one of its horns and hurled him ahead.

McDaniel broke his femur, the strongest bone in the body, in four places near his hip.



An X-ray revealed the extent of what his doctor described as a “pretty painful injury.”

“We saw the bison and he was down,” McDaniel said from his hospital bed.

“He wasn’t showing signs of aggression… until it picked a target. That target happened to be me.

“At the time, I had my grandson with me… They move master that you ever imagine.



“He just kept coming and he was aggressive. And as soon as he got off that tree, he launched me in the air.

“I didn’t get bruises from him launching me in the air, but it was the landing that became the problem.”

McDaniel explained that his family had just finished eating dinner and he was out on a walk with his grandson when the attack took place.

He warned his grandson to get to safety and tried to run from the bison himself, but it continued to chase after him.

“Even though I was on the ground, he could’ve stomped me, he could’ve gored me, he could’ve done anything,” he added.



McDaniel said he is grateful to have survived the attack and believed his injuries could have been worse.

Pointing at the X-ray, his doctor explained that his bone is actually broken in “multiple pieces.”

“You can see some fragments here and there are fractures and break lines right through that,” he added.

Professional photographer Mike MacLeod captured the extraordinary incident on film, claiming that the victim was “in good spirits” as soon as the ordeal was over.

“He was in a lot of pain, but was conscious and joking the whole time,” he told Cowboy State Daily.



“He was really worried and wanted to see the video to make sure it wasn’t his fault.

“It’s not his fault. You can tell from the very beginning. That was a really, really angry bison.”

Prior to Carl’s near-death experience, the bison had already terrorised several other groups of visitors.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In the aftermath, Yellowstone National Park told The Sun: “A 65-year-old man was injured by a bison on the evening of July 10 at Bridge Bay Campground near Lake Yellowstone in Yellowstone National Park.

“Park emergency medical personnel responded and transported him to a nearby hospital.”

News.title: Brit tourist, 60, drowns after being swept out to sea as his heartbroken family fume ‘lifeguards were slow to respond’
News.content:
OCEAN TRAGEDY Brit tourist, 60, drowns after being swept out to sea as his heartbroken family fume ‘lifeguards were slow to respond’

A BRITISH dad has drowned after being swept away to sea as his heartbroken family claim the lifeguards were too slow to respond.

The holidaymaker, 60, had been swimming in Cancun, Mexico with his two children when the tragedy unfolded.



Desperate onlookers began calling for help when they spotted the family battling the strong currents on Friday afternoon.

The area where the dad and his kids had entered opposite Nyx Hotel had been flying a red flag – a signal to swimmers for choppy seas.



The two youngsters, whose ages have not been revealed, were rescued alive.

But their father was hauled ashore unconscious – and later pronounced dead at the scene.



Devastated relatives accused the beach lifeguards of acting too slowly to rescue the Brit and his children, reported Mexican newspaper Por Esto.

They said that when they saw the father struggling in the water they begged a rescuer to intervene – but that their pleas were ignored.

It was only some moments later that a second lifeguard dove in to help the victims.

Officials have not yet made any comment about the alleged failings in the lifeguard service.



Police have launched an investigation into the incident.

The names of the father and his children have not yet been made public.

The popular tourist hotspot was cordoned off as ambulances and police swarmed the area.

Harrowing photos show the body lying on the beach covered by a blue blanket.

The beach where the British holidaymaker died is called San Miguelito Beach and is described as one of the best in Cancun.



One local insisted today: “Hoteles should warn guests about how dangerous going into the sea can be.”

Another said: “You come here on holiday and go home without your father. How sad.”

News.title: Britain is crying out for a leader, not a people-pleaser – Angry voters will be quick to punish Burnham if he fails
News.content:
No easy fixes

AFTER becoming our unelected Prime Minister yesterday, Andy Burnham said his generation of politicians needed to “raise our game”.

Unfortunately for the hard workers and wealth-creators of this country, one of his first acts might well be to raise their taxes.



The new PM yesterday repeated some of his high-spending vision: building tens of thousands of council houses, state control of energy and water and “re-industrialising” Britain using vast sums of taxpayers’ cash.

How he is going to pay for his ten-year plan — which, staggeringly, won’t be set out for months — remains to be seen.



Having celebrated in Downing Street with his Northern supporters, Burnham later refused to rule out increasing the top rate of income tax to 50p.

Despite that being a policy that has historically led to SMALLER tax receipts for the Treasury, he believes it could help pay for a lifting of thresholds for low-income taxpayers.



But experts reckon that could cost up to £5billion while delivering a saving to poorer workers of just £100 a year.

It falls to new Chancellor John Healey to make these difficult sums add up.

He must ensure the class-war politics of envy, which run deep in Burnham’s team — led by his de facto Deputy PM, the virulently left-wing Louise Haigh — don’t trump economic reality.

There will be widespread relief on the markets at Healey’s shock return to the Treasury at the expense of Ed Miliband, now made Foreign Secretary. It should also be good news for defence chiefs desperate for cash to re-arm.



But beyond the smiles and Manchester vibes, there are serious problems ahead.

The public have been clear for years about their priorities: cutting welfare, stopping the boats and fixing our broken borders system.

They are sick of paying sky-high taxes, believe Net Zero is failing and want more NEW drilling in the North Sea.

And they are fed up with political chaos delivering our seventh PM in just over a decade.

Has Burnham got the stomach to deliver any of this? More than half his party hates the idea of slashing welfare — the only way to find the money to mend our public services.



Instead, the fantasists on his backbenches want to soak the strivers with MORE tax to pay for reforms.

Meanwhile most Labour MPs want open borders and are hostile to Shabana Mahmood’s tough immigration reforms.

By purging almost every Starmer loyalist minister yesterday, Burnham may have also undermined his own promise to end infighting in the party.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Britain is crying out for a leader, not a people-pleaser.

Tinkering with bus fares and chucking £340million at ending rough sleeping is unlikely to cut it with angry voters, who will be quick to punish Burnham if he fails.

News.title: Andy Burnham launches brutal Cabinet bloodbath with Starmer allies purged as Rayner returns & Healey becomes Chancellor
News.content:
ANDY Burnham executed a brutal purge of Sir Keir Starmer’s Cabinet allies in his first move at No10.

The new Prime Minister shocked Westminster yesterday by revealing John Healey as his Chancellor after ­sacking Rachel Reeves.



Eco-crusading Ed Miliband had been gunning for the Treasury job — but was instead packed off abroad as Foreign Secretary.

Shabana Mahmood remained as Home Secretary to ­continue pushing through her immigration reforms.



Ms Reeves was one of the loyalists of outgoing PM Sir Keir Starmer who were pushed out as Mr Burnham cleared the decks on his first day in Downing Street.

Other casualties included David Lammy, Lord Hermer, Peter Kyle, Steve Reed, Liz Kendall, Nick Thomas-Symonds, Darren Jones, Jo ­Stevens and Hilary Benn.

They made way for Mr Burnham’s pals including comebacks for Angela Rayner and Louise Haigh — who were both forced to resign during Sir Keir’s tenure.

Ms Rayner, who quit in September over stamp duty on her flat in Hove, East Sussex, is back as Housing Secretary.



Ms Haigh departed in November 2024 after her fraud conviction was revealed.

She has now become Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster.

But the biggest surprise was the appointment of Mr Healey as Chancellor — only a month after he had quit as Defence Secretary in a dispute over military spending.



Downing Street sources said he was chosen as he shares Mr Burnham’s approach to the economy, combining fiscal discipline with investment to drive growth and regenerate industrial communities.

They also pointed to past ­Treasury experience under Gordon Brown when he was Chancellor, serving for five years as Economic Secretary and Financial Secretary.

Mr Healey said it was “time to get on with the job”.

He vowed to work in “lockstep” with Mr Burnham to meet strict fiscal rules and help in the cost-of-living fight.

Mr Healey added: “Fiscal control is the first duty of any Chancellor — it is mine — and fiscal credibility is the bedrock . . . for economic stability and for national security.



“You heard the Prime Minister this afternoon say, in this more dangerous world, we will meet our commitments on defence to our international allies.”

He now faces the task of finding the billions needed to deliver Mr Burnham’s defence promises without breaking Labour’s fiscal rules.

Late last night Wes Streeting was named Defence Secretary, succeeding Dan Jarvis who was in the role for less than six weeks.

Team Burnham was frustrated to discover that £4.7billion of the £15billion defence spending uplift was unfunded.

Yvette Cooper was demoted from Foreign Secretary to make way for Mr Miliband, becoming the Health Secretary instead.



Lucy Powell was made Education Secretary, with her divisive predecessor Bridget Phillipson demoted to keeping only part of her brief, remaining Minister for Women and Equalities.

Pat McFadden is staying as Welfare Secretary to sort out the crippling benefits bill, while Lisa Nandy stays as Culture Secretary.

Jonathan Reynolds returned to his old role as Business Secretary, and little-known Anneliese Midgley was named Chief Whip.

Ed Miliband’s protégée Miatta Fahnbulleh takes over from him as Energy Secretary.

Angela Eagle was named Environment Secretary and Alex Norris Justice Secretary.



In his first speech outside Downing Street, Mr Burnham had promised “a ­circuit breaker for Britain”.

He said his Government would bring forward “the biggest changes in the last 40 years” through “a new political model and a new economic model”.

But he acknowledged that his ten-year plan for delivering that transformation would not be unveiled until later this year.

He instead promised there would be immediate action on the cost-of-living crisis.

He said ­families would get “some breathing space” when he announces his first measures and explains “how we pay for them”.



The former Mayor of Greater Manchester also pledged education reforms, better mental health ­support for young people, more council homes and to end rough sleeping in England.

Ms Mahmood retained the Home Office after narrowly missing out on the Treasury.

Sources close to Ms Mahmood insisted she made clear in the reshuffle process that she wanted to remain in the Home Secretary role.

They said she would now focus on delivering the Government’s pledge to make Britain’s streets safer and create a fairer immigration system.

Yet the scale of the bloodbath left little doubt Mr Burnham wanted a clean break from the Starmer era.



Ms Reeves insisted it had been “the privilege of my life” to serve as Chancellor.

It is understood she was offered a significant job but decided to turn it down.

Former Deputy Prime Minister Mr Lammy said he would have been “proud” to continue serving in Cabinet, but accepted that “a new Prime Minister is entitled to build his own team” and pledged to support the Government from the backbenches.

But former Housing Secretary Steve Reed used his resignation letter to deliver a pointed message to Mr Burnham over his coup.

He wrote: “I hope those who did not show loyalty to Keir will now show it to you.”



Mr Reed also urged him not to overlook southern voters, warning Labour must govern for the whole country if it is to earn a second term in office.

Mr Burnham had been joined by his family for his arrival.

His wife, Dutch-born Marie-France van Heel, was with him outside No10, and he also hugged his mum Eileen.

OUT

MINISTERS bid farewell to Sir Keir Starmer outside Downing Street yesterday. With many losing their jobs, too.

RECOMMENDED STORIES





IN

PRIME Minister Andy Burnham welcomes his new Chancellor of the Exchequer, former Defence ­Secretary John ­Healey, inside No10 — the first appointment of the re­shuffled ­Cabinet.

News.title: ‘Pure evil’ boy, 16, stabbed accountant, 26, to death with machete in ambush after he ‘pestered’ girl for sex
News.content:
A “PURE evil” boy stabbed an accountant to death with a machete after luring him for sex with a 16-year-old girl.

Emmanuel Avogo, then 16, hatched a plan with a girl to “lure” Adam Khan, 26, to a meeting in Luton.



When Khan arrived at Humberstone Road, Avogo chased after him and pulled out a machete before stabbing him.

After being convicted at a murder trial, the boy, now 17, has been handed a life sentence.



Harrow Crown Court heard that Khan had been “pestering” the girl for sex and agreed to provide her with some cannabis.

The girl, who could not be named, planned an attack with Avogo, but she did not know he would be armed with the machete.

CCTV footage of the incident from August 31, 2025, shows Khan approaching a car and talking to the girl through the window.

Suddenly Avogo confronts Khan and pulls out a machete from his trousers.



The accountant retreats into his car and drives away for a short distance with the boy chasing after him.

He stops his vehicle to take a tyre wrench from the boot to face Avogo with.

Khan was stabbed five times – in the face, stomach and arm – in the fight that followed, and died later that evening in hospital.

The judge said: “By August 31 he had offered to get you some cannabis for some form of sexual favour, and most people would agree this was very wrong.

“It would have served him right if you two had taken the drugs and run off, but he had done nothing to deserve the terrible violence done to him that day.”



Khan’s sister dubbed the killers “pure evil” and told them to “rot in hell” as the court heard how the victim had been destined for a successful career as an accountant when he was killed.

On Monday, Avogo was sentenced to life with a minimum term of 20 years.

The girl was sentenced to a two-year detention and training order after she was found guilty at trial of manslaughter.

The court also heard that Avogo regularly carried a knife and had a past involving knives and violence.

The teen had been spared jail, four months before confronting Khan, after stabbing a man with a 67cm-long machete during the robbery of an e-bike.



In 2023, he attempted to push another boy into the road and punching him in the face and also attacked two fellow school pupils.

Avogo also assaulted a police officer in January 2024, and he was caught with a lock knife in August that year, when aged 15.

The judge added: “The seriousness of the offence of which he was convicted and the widespread publicity and concern surrounding young people and knife crime militate in favour of allowing this case to be examined by the press and discussed by the public.”

He stripped Avogo of his anonymity after the Press Association applied to be able to name him as a deterrent against knife crime.

Khan’s mother, who was not named, told the court that her son had started working at 15 after the death of his father to support his family, and she called him “bright, strong, resilient and caring”.



She said of the teenage killers: “I hope they meet a fate far worse than what they inflicted on my son.”

Khan’s sister said that her brother was murdered a day before he was due to take his final accountancy qualification exam, having got himself a job within a top financial firm.

“He had so much to look forward to, but that was brutally snatched from him,” she said.

She said the teenage killers have “pure evil inside of them”, and said: “My brother’s death will hover over our heads and leave a hole in our hearts for the rest of our lives.”

She added: “I pray the harshest of justice is served to the inhumane people who committed this crime.



“May they rot in hell.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Avogo blamed the PTSD he got after being hit in the head with a hammer and having surgery in 2023 as contributing to his confrontation with Khan.

Mr Justice Bennathan noted that the boy continues to plead his innocence over Khan’s death, insisting he had not intended to cause him serious harm.

News.title: Andy Burnham live: Prime Minister scraps VAT on household electricity bills ahead of first Cabinet meeting
News.content:
New Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has announced cuts VAT on household electricity bills ahead of Cabinet meeting - the move is expected to take around £45 off the yearly Ofgem price cap

Watch in full: Andy Burnham delivers his first speech as Prime Minister

Andy Burnham has announced VAT cuts on household electricity bills ahead of his first Cabinet meeting today.

In his first speech as PM yesterday, Andy Burnham said an announcement about tackling the cost of living would be made today. He said he could "do something to give people some breathing space now" and was looking at measures "that could make a difference this year".

The tax cut is set to remove VAT from domestic electricity bills from October 1 in time to impact the next Ofgem price cap. The new Prime Minister says the move will "put more money in people's pockets and bring back hope".

Andy Burnham begins his first full day as Prime Minister today with a cabinet meeting this morning. His team includes John Healey as chancellor, Shabana Mahmood as home secretary, and Ed Miliband as foreign secretary.
