World.title: Iraq reaches major agricultural milestone with first Super S potato seeds
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — The Iraqi Ministry of Agriculture has achieved a major scientific and strategic breakthrough, marking a first for the nation’s agricultural sector. On Monday, July 20, 2026, the ministry officially announced that its Department of Horticulture successfully produced “Super S” grade potato seeds—the highest internationally recognized classification for potato seed quality.

The milestone was confirmed after the locally developed seeds passed exhaustive rigorous testing conducted by the Seed Testing and Certification Department, proving their absolute alignment with top global standards.

The strategic project was executed under the auspices of Minister of Agriculture Abdul Rahim Al-Shammari and directly supervised by the Director General of the Horticulture Department, Hatem Karim Al-Ghazi. The production represents the culmination of years of intensive research and practical field applications managed by the technical and scientific cadres of the National Potato Development Program.

Specialized operations spanned multiple laboratory and field stations, relying heavily on the Tissue Culture Unit in Nineveh Governorate and the Upper Euphrates Station in Anbar Governorate to ensure the harvest of genetically pure, disease-free, and virus-free national seed stocks.

Strategic Impact of the National “Super S” Seed Production

Securing Food Sovereignty: Establishing the local production of this top global seed classification acts as a foundational step toward building a sustainable, entirely domestic system for potato cultivation inside Iraq.

Reducing Import Reliance: The initiative directly aims to limit the country’s dependence on expensive imported foreign seeds, granting the agricultural sector greater autonomy over an essential crop.

Boosting the National Economy: Transitioning to domestic production will dramatically lower overall cultivation costs for local farmers while saving vital hard currency reserves that were previously spent on international seed procurement.

Maximizing Crop Yields: The high genetic purity and complete absence of viral strains inherent in “Super S” seeds directly optimize agricultural efficiency, significantly raising the production output per dunam.

This pivotal shift in seed infrastructure serves as a major pillar supporting the sustainable development strategies that the Ministry of Agriculture aims to replicate across other primary food crops.

The tangible results of this achievement are projected to positively impact local markets over the coming harvest seasons, offering Iraqi consumers and farmers a premium, highly competitive national product that stabilizes the domestic supply chain.

World.title: The Tehran test: PM Al Zaidi to demand militia disarmament in Iran visit
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Fresh off his diplomatic trip to Washington and a brief stopover in Doha, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi is preparing to land in Tehran on July 23, 2026. The high-stakes visit, highlighted in an analytical report by Al-Mada newspaper, is being viewed as the ultimate litmus test for the sovereign promises al-Zaidi made directly to U.S. President Donald Trump regarding domestic stability and the rule of law.

While historical precedent has typically seen Tehran serve as the mandatory protocol stop for incoming Iraqi prime ministers immediately following a White House invite, al-Zaidi’s itinerary carries deep tactical friction. Well-informed political sources reveal that the Prime Minister will formally ask the Iranian leadership to exert direct, decisive pressure on its allied domestic armed factions to surrender what intelligence circles call the “ballistic card.”

Specifically, Baghdad is demanding that these non-state groups hand over a hidden arsenal estimated to include at least eight ballistic missiles and hundreds of kamikaze drones before the September 30 legal deadline set by the federal cabinet to permanently eradicate unauthorized weapons.

High-Stakes Geopolitical Itinerary: Post-Washington Matrix

The Disarmament Deadline: September 30 remains the definitive federal cutoff for independent armed factions to integrate or fully surrender heavy arms to state control.

The Hidden Arsenal: Intelligence estimates indicate that renegade factions continue to conceal hundreds of localized drones alongside at least 8 Iranian-supplied ballistic missiles.

The Diplomatic Pre-Run: Preparations peaked in Baghdad on Monday, July 20, as Deputy Foreign Minister Muhammad Hussein Bahr al-Uloom met with Iranian Ambassador Iraj Masjedi to iron out the security agenda.

The Shifting Route: Al-Zaidi adjusted his post-US economic tour, inserting Doha and Tehran ahead of upcoming investment summits in Turkey (July 28) and Saudi Arabia to address the security crisis first.

The political stakes for the Prime Minister could not be higher. During his five days in the United States, al-Zaidi secured forty-eight monumental agreements and memorandums of understanding valued at nearly $60 billion—spanning energy deals with Chevron and ExxonMobil, digital infrastructure with Starlink, and an initial compliance framework with the U.S. Treasury to rehabilitate seven restricted domestic banks.

However, diplomatic experts and strategic analysts, including Ihsan Al-Shammari, a professor of international politics at Baghdad University, warn that any failure by al-Zaidi to decisively strip these rogue factions of their heavy weapons will trigger immediate economic blowback from Washington, potentially freezing the multi-billion-dollar corporate contracts.

Al-Shammari pointed out that the volatile drone and missile strikes launched against the Kurdistan Region late Friday night were not merely extensions of the broader U.S.–Iran conflict, but functioned as “preemptive rejection messages” from hardline local factions aiming to destabilize al-Zaidi’s administration.

Intelligence reports obtained by Al-Mada suggest that Baghdad is already moving toward a highly anticipated anti-terror sweep codenamed the “Decisive Operation.” The federal government has reportedly finalized arrest warrants for the specific factional leaders behind the recent Erbil and Sulaymaniyah breaches, vowing to publicly broadcast their identities and utilize proactive preemptive detentions if renegade cells attempt to target foreign oil conglomerates, diplomatic missions, or state bases in the coming days.

World.title: Scars of war linger on Syria’s Saint Simeon monastery
World.content:
Dayr Sim’ān – Near the base of a column atop which Saint Simeon Stylites once perched, scattered stones lay bare the damage inflicted on the surrounding Byzantine monastery in northern Syria by war, looting and rampant illegal excavations.

AFP accompanied a French archaeological delegation to inspect the site after more than a decade of conflict and assess what could be restored.

The fifth-century monastery and its church are, alongside hundreds of abandoned ancient villages in northern Syria known as the “dead” or “forgotten cities”, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Holding her camera and notebook, archaeologist Micheline Kurdi walked through the ruins to document the site’s state and plan the first “quick interventions” to restore it, she told AFP.

“There is irreparable damage in the monastery in the southeastern section, but on the other hand the church is standing firm and in good condition,” the 42-year-old French-Syrian said.

Inside the monastery, AFP journalists saw cracked arches and partially collapsed stone walls, while the monks’ living quarters remained intact.

– ‘Rebuild it’ –

Syria was once an archaeologist’s paradise, home to some of the oldest and best-preserved jewels of ancient civilisations.

Following the start of the civil war in 2011, archaeological sites across the country were damaged, museums looted and historic city centres levelled.

One of the most famous cases was Palmyra, the Roman-era city in Syria’s desert with an imposing kilometre-long colonnade, where the Islamic State jihadist group launched a campaign of destruction and looting after capturing the site in 2015.

The Saint Simeon monastery itself was subjected to “looting, illegal excavation, military use and neglect”, according to site director Abdel Jalil Arabi.

It was controlled by various armed groups throughout the war, he said.

An airstrike hit the monastery in 2016, which UNESCO condemned without naming the party responsible, while it was further damaged by a major earthquake in 2023.

Arabi estimated that 30 to 40 percent of the site has been damaged, pointing to the collapse of the western arch and its columns.

As for Saint Simeon’s column, Arabi said “the base is there, but the remains of the column are scattered, and we will try to rebuild it”.

The monastery, which includes one of the oldest major churches in Christianity, was built around a column that Saint Simeon sat on for years, dedicating his life to prayer.

Kurdi, who dedicated her doctoral thesis to the monastery complex, said they needed to “review old plans” to reinstall the base of the main column “and the part that remained of it”.

– Past and future –

Jean-Baptiste Faivre, French charge d’affaires in Syria, said “this heritage is extremely important, not only for Syria’s past but also for its future”.

“There will be cooperation between the Syrian Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums and French cultural institutions to help restore and develop this site.”

Vincent Gelot from the French Catholic organisation Oeuvre d’Orient, who was also at the site, said the restoration would be carried out “with the support of donors and our partners, such as the French Embassy and the Aliph Foundation, which works to protect heritage in war-affected countries”.

“We hope that tourists and pilgrims will one day return to this place, because it still carries a message and speaks to us even today,” he added.

World.title: Plane carrying Spain’s World Cup winning team lands in Madrid
World.content:
Madrid – A plane carrying Spain’s newly crowned World Cup champions landed in Madrid on Monday, a day after their 1-0 victory over Argentina in the final in the United States.

A Spanish flag fluttered from the cockpit window as the Iberia aircraft carrying the squad taxied to the terminal at Madrid-Barajas airport at 14:30 local time (12:30 GMT) under clear blue skies.

Coach Luis de la Fuente was the first to step off the plane, followed by player of the tournament Rodri, who held the World Cup trophy aloft at the top of the stairs.

The squad were due to meet King Felipe VI at Zarzuela Palace outside Madrid before heading to the government headquarters at Moncloa Palace for a reception with Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez.

The players and coaching staff will then parade through central Madrid on an open-top bus before arriving at the Cibeles square where a ceremony will be held.

Around one million people are expected to flood the streets of the Spanish capital to salute the players.

World.title: Iraqi forces destroy six ISIS hideouts in Kirkuk
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi military announced on Monday that Iraqi security forces had identified and destroyed six suspected hideouts belonging to ISIS in the northern province of Kirkuk during an air operation.

Iraq’s Joint Operations Command said in a statement that an airborne group of Special Forces carried out a rapid security operation early on Monday.

The hideouts were destroyed in precise airstrikes after field operations identified them in the Zghitun Valley area in Kirkuk, according to the statement.

The Kurdistan Region Security Agency (Asayish) also announced the arrest of two suspected ISIS militants in separate operations coordinated with Iraq’s Counter-Terrorism Service (CTS) in Sulaymaniyah province earlier in July.

In 2014, the terrorist group ISIS took control of large areas in Iraq and Syria before being defeated in 2017.

Over five million Iraqis had to flee the governorates of Nineveh, Salah al-Din, parts of Kirkuk, Diyala, and Anbar because of ISIS control over these areas in 2014.

Although Iraq declared in late 2017 that all of its regions were free of ISIS, the government continues to conduct security operations to hunt out any remaining members of the terrorist group.

World.title: Economist: Dollar return is out of reach for restricted Iraqi banks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Prominent economic expert Ziad Al-Hashemi issued a sobering analysis on Monday, July 20, 2026, regarding the recent joint understanding between the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI) and the U.S. Department of the Treasury.

Al-Hashemi cautioned that the official statements do not imply an imminent return to U.S. dollar transactions for the restricted Iraqi financial institutions, describing full dollar integration as currently “out of reach” due to stringent compliance benchmarks.

The critique follows an announcement by the Central Bank of Iraq and a welcoming statement from Prime Minister Ali Falih al-Zaidi regarding a framework to qualify seven restricted Iraqi banks for a return to international correspondent banking channels.

While the government celebrated the milestone as a major leap forward for global financial integration, Al-Hashemi emphasized that the U.S. Treasury has explicitly conditioned the lifting of restrictions on a series of rigorous structural reforms that remain far from complete.

According to Al-Hashemi’s assessment of the official U.S. Treasury declaration, the transition for these restricted institutions will be heavily phased and contingent on challenging corporate governance overhauls:

Alternative Currencies Only: The initial phase of the agreement only explores re-integrating select banks into global correspondent networks using non-dollar currencies, such as the Euro, UAE Dirham, and Chinese Yuan.

Lack of American Correspondent Partners: To date, no restricted Iraqi bank has regained the ability to conduct foreign currency transactions, primarily because major U.S. banking institutions refuse to establish correspondent relationships with them.

The Structural Phase One: The first phase of the CBI-led banking reform initiative is scheduled to conclude this summer, but eligibility for alternative currencies remains strictly tied to meeting baseline governance and compliance standards.

The Stringent Path to the Dollar: To eventually handle U.S. dollars, banks must successfully complete all subsequent reform phases, pass a satisfactory third-party audit of their compliance functions, attract a qualified institutional investor, and meet international standards regarding professional competence, integrity, and fitness.

Ownership Restructuring Barriers: Domestic banks view these extensive conditions as exceptionally difficult to implement, with the U.S. Treasury’s strict mandates regarding bank ownership percentages posing the most significant structural hurdle.

Citing the formal documentation, Al-Hashemi highlighted the explicit security guardrails embedded within Washington’s fiscal policy toward Baghdad: “The United States will not tolerate the abuse of Iraqi banks by armed groups allied with Iran, and will take independent action, when necessary, to target such activities.”

Al-Hashemi noted that the primary misconception in the local market stems from confusing the allowance of alternative currency clearing with the lifting of the actual U.S. dollar ban. He asserted that it is highly improbable for these seven banks to enter the U.S. dollar transfer system over the short or medium term.

Beyond the lack of acceptance from institutional U.S. correspondent banks, the restricted Iraqi financial firms have failed to fully implement the comprehensive restructuring requirements mandated by the global consulting firm Oliver Wyman. The Oliver Wyman plan serves as the core technical benchmark for the Central Bank of Iraq’s broader strategy to modernize the domestic financial sector, increase corporate transparency, and combat money laundering and illicit financial flows.

Until these foundational auditing and ownership criteria are completely satisfied, Al-Hashemi concludes that the financial integration celebrated during the Washington summit will remain an idealized roadmap rather than an immediate commercial reality.

World.title: Ryanair quarterly profit slides on Mideast war impact
World.content:
London – Irish no-frills airline Ryanair on Monday said net profit slumped 34 percent in its first quarter as the Middle East conflict sent jet-fuel prices soaring and impacted ticket sales.

Profit after tax dropped to 538 million euros ($616 million) in the three months to the end of June, from 820 million euros one year earlier, the Dublin-based carrier said in a statement.

Ryanair, which is Europe’s biggest airline by passenger numbers and flies mainly across the continent, said the cost of fuel not subject to advance purchase agreements had soared owing to the US-Iran war.

“Operating costs rose 11 percent to 3.81 billion euros as the price of our 20-percent unhedged jet-fuel more than doubled” in the first quarter, chief executive Michael O’Leary said in the earnings statement.

While passenger traffic grew six percent, fares dropped six percent.

Fares “required stimulation as the Middle East conflict led to consumer hesitancy, concerns about EU jet-fuel shortages, economic uncertainty and later bookings”, O’Leary said.

He added that Ryanair’s net profit for the remainder of its financial year “remains highly sensitive to… conflict escalation in the Middle East and Ukraine, the price of unhedged jet-fuel, macro-economic shocks” and European air traffic control strikes.

Ryanair’s share price slid nearly six percent in Dublin midday trading after investors reacted to the bigger-than-expected drop in profits.

The airline’s “results show just how quickly nervousness surrounding the war has seeped into booking patterns and operational costs”, noted Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at Wealth Club.

“It’s a sign that consumers are once again tightening their belts and delaying discretionary spending, leaving airlines exposed not just to soaring jet fuel costs but also the prospect of softer demand.”

World.title: Iraq leads Gulf oil exports growth despite Hormuz crisis
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq was one of the main drivers of the increase in crude oil exports from the Gulf region during the first half of July, according to shipping firms Kpler and Vortexa.

This development comes at a time when oil export levels from the region were at their peak since the outbreak of the US-Iran war in late February, despite reduced tankers’ movements in the Strait of Hormuz due to increased military operations.

Oil exports from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Iraq, Kuwait, and Iran increased by roughly 16 percent compared to June, hitting approximately 12 million barrels per day, according to Kpler, while Vortexa estimated the figure at 13.06 million barrels per day.

Iraq experienced the largest increase in oil shipments among the Gulf countries during that period, contributing significantly to the overall growth in crude exports alongside Saudi Arabia and Iran, according to Vortexa.

Despite this improvement, Reuters noted that oil shipments from the Gulf region are still approximately 32 percent below their pre-war level of 17.6 million barrels per day in February.

The number of oil tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz plummeted to three on a single day, the lowest level since May, raising fears about growing tensions and potential threats to Red Sea commerce, which might affect global oil flows.

World.title: 'Future of youth priority': PM Modi says NEET leak national issue, avoid 'partisan politics'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union minister

Tuesday said PM Narendra Modi, during the NDA's parliamentary party meeting, retierated government's stance to ensure "stringent punishment" for those involved in the NEET paper leak.

Rijiju, who is the minister of parliamentary affairs, said the Prime Minister stated that "NEET paper leak should not be an issue of partisan politics".

PM Modi, according to Rijiju, also said that "security and future of youth" is the government's priority.

The Prime Minister's reaction comes in the backdrop of youth, led by Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), protesting against the perpetual paper leaks, and alleged irregularities in the education system.

The uproar over the NEET leak and lack of accountablity at the senior-most level exploded in the Captial on Monday as protestors, mostly students and youths, clashed with police -- leading the cops to resort to lathi charge, firing of tear gas to disperse the protesting crowd marching towards the Parliament.

The protestors had three main demands: Resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, discharging Sonam Wangchuk from hospital and providing compensation to the kin of NEET aspirants who died by suicide after the leak forced the government to reexamination.





The Monday mayhem



Many of those brought to both hospitals were discharged after receiving first aid.

Officials at RML said that by 7 pm, the hospital's surgery department had registered 65 medico-legal cases (MLCs) involving both protesters and police personnel. They added that detailed information on all cases was still being compiled.

Hospital authorities also said around 10 MLCs involved people who had been on hunger strike.

All of them were reported to be in stable condition.

Sources at RML said nearly 40 of the injured brought to the hospital were police personnel, while the remaining patients were protesters. Around 35 people were admitted, with the rest treated and discharged. Between seven and eight patients required treatment in the hospital's red zone because of the seriousness of their injuries.

Among those admitted was a 20-year-old woman who suffered a hypoxic brain injury, a condition caused when the brain is deprived of adequate oxygen following severe trauma, hospital sources said.

The exact circumstances in which she sustained her injuries remain unclear. According to hospital sources, she may have been injured during the clashes or after falling in the stampede that followed, but the sequence of events has not yet been established.

Doctors said most of the remaining patients suffered bruises, baton injuries, head wounds and facial injuries, including split lips, forehead wounds and scalp lacerations.

Although many had visible injuries to the head and face, no fractures were reported among patients treated at RML.

At Lady Hardinge Medical College, at least 24 injured people were treated. Most were discharged after first aid, while those who arrived later in the evening continued to undergo medical evaluation. Doctors at the hospital said none of the patients brought there had sustained major injuries.

World.title: India summons Russian diplomat over 4 Indians killed in strike off Ukranian coast
World.content:
Four Indian nationals were killed after a commercial vessel, MV Golden Leo, came under attac.

NEW DELHI: India on Tuesday summoned Russian diplomat over the killing of four Indians on board a merchant vessel off the coast of Ukraine, reported news agency PTI citing sources.Four Indian nationals were killed after a commercial vessel, MV Golden Leo, came under attack while departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on Sunday, the Indian government confirmed. One more Indian crew member remains in critical condition.According to the government, the vessel had 17 crew members on board, including five Indian nationals, when it was attacked.India strongly condemned the strike, saying attacks on commercial shipping and civilian crew members were unacceptable.India, in a statement, said, âAs per the information available, four Indian nationals have tragically lost their lives, while one is hospitalised in a critical condition. Our mission in Ukraine is closely monitoring the situation and is making every effort to extend all possible assistance to those affected.âThe government also reiterated that targeting commercial vessels, endangering civilian seafarers and disrupting freedom of navigation and international trade was deplorable and should be avoided.One of those killed has been identified as 26-year-old merchant navy officer Akhil Joyan from Vellarikkundu in Kerala's Kasaragod district. His family was informed of his death by the shipping company through an email on Monday.Akhil had recently returned home on leave, got engaged and had resumed duty only a month ago.According to a Reuters report, Ukrainian officials said a Russian missile strike hit a ship carrying corn near the southern port of Odesa, killing 10 people.

World.title: Wangchuk continues to refuse IV fluids despite medical advice; low blood sugar, potassium persist
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Climate activist

continues to decline intravenous fluids and glucose administration despite repeated medical advice, even as his blood sugar levels remained on the lower side, serum potassium dropped to 3.2 mEq/L and laboratory tests showed persistent pancytopenia, a condition marked by reduced blood cell counts, according to the latest health bulletin issued by VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital on Tuesday morning.

The hospital said Wangchuk's vital parameters remain stable, but he continues to have persistent pancytopenia, characterised by anaemia and low leukocyte (white blood cell) counts. These clinical and laboratory findings warrant continued close monitoring through serial investigations, it said.

Doctors said Wangchuk is currently receiving oral rehydration therapy (ORS) and oral potassium supplementation.

However, he continues to refuse intravenous fluids and glucose administration despite repeated medical advice.

According to the bulletin, Wangchuk remains under the close supervision of a multidisciplinary team of experts from VMMC & Safdarjung Hospital and AIIMS, New Delhi. In view of his ongoing mild to moderate dehydration, persistent laboratory abnormalities and the physiological stress associated with prolonged fasting, sustained medical supervision and continuous clinical monitoring remain essential for his recovery and for the timely identification and management of any potential complications, it said.





The hospital said all necessary medical care is being provided and Wangchuk's clinical condition remains under close and continuous assessment. Further management will be guided by his clinical progress and serial laboratory investigations.

World.title: 'Truck carrying Abhijeet Dipke, Gitanjali, Shabana Azmi, Prakash Raj brutally attacked': CJP accuses Delhi Police of violence
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), the pressure group leading the ongoing protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar, on Tuesday levelled serious allegations of police brutality during its march to Parliament a day earlier, claiming that several protesters, including well-known public figures, were assaulted.

The internet-sensation-turned-pressure group alleged that actors

and

, along with

's wife Gitanjali and CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke, were inside a truck that was "brutally attacked" by the police.

In a post on X, the CJP's official handle said, "CJP Founder Abhijeet Dipke, Gitanjali ji (Sonam sirâs wife), actors Shabana Azmi and Prakash Raj were all in this truck which the Police brutally attacked.

They dragged one protester who was helping to navigate and chased him to beat him up. The Police thought we will get scared - but they are wrong!

Ladenge jeetenge!

"

Adding to the allegations, CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that Gitanjali, wife of educationist and activist Sonam Wangchuk, was dragged out of the vehicle by her hair during the police action.

Recounting Monday's protest, Ranka said, "It was just the Police who used lathis. Our youths were beaten up, their heads cracked open, they were dragged on streets. Sonam sir's wife Gitanjali ma'am's hair was pulled in order to drag her out of truck...Ribs of one of our volunteers was shattered. We had never expected or seen such brutality. Delhi Police crossed all limits yesterday. Clearly, they were given instructions to beat up people.





But this will further expand the protest. More number of people will come to Delhi. We will not move from here until Dharmendra Pradhan resigns."

Ranka also expressed disappointment over the outcome of Monday's meeting with the government, saying, "We did not receive any response. 5 hours were wasted. If the Govt wants to talk to us, they will now have to come here."

Meanwhile, the Delhi Police rejected the allegations, saying the claims made by the CJP were false and misleading.

In a statement, the Delhi Police said, "False information is being currently circulated on social media regarding the posts claim that an individual named Geetanjali, a 12-year-old girl was assaulted, had her hair pulled, sustained a head injury, and approximately 40 to 50 other individuals suffered broken heads. This information is false. The claims being circulated in the posts are not true..."

However, in a first formal engagement with the Centre since the protest began, CJP representatives met Union health minister Jagat Prakash Nadda on Monday.

Following the meeting, CJP spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka claimed that Nadda had sought more time to consult the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leadership on the group's demands before responding.

World.title: Kerala merchant navy man dies in Russian strike off Ukraine ahead of wedding
World.content:
Russian strike kills 26-year-old Kerala merchant navy man off Ukraine coast

NEW DELHI: A 26-year-old man from Kerala working in the merchant navy was killed after the cargo vessel he was serving on allegedly came under a Russian strike off the Ukrainian coast, people close to his family said on Monday.His death came just two months before he was due to get married.The deceased, Akhil Joyan, was the only son of Joyan and Sally, residents of Vellarikkundu in Kerala's Kasaragod district.Shobi Joseph, ward member of Vellarikkundu in Balal grama panchayat, told PTI that the family received an email from the shipping company informing them of Akhil's death on Monday evening."We are trying to gather more details and complete the necessary formalities. He joined the merchant navy at the age of 19," Joseph said.According to Joseph, Akhil had returned to his hometown around three months ago for his engagement ceremony."His marriage was scheduled to take place two months from now. The bride is from Alappuzha district. He returned to work a month back," he said.Joseph described Akhil as a well-known and respected figure in the locality, who was also a popular tug-of-war player."He was known as a well-behaved and disciplined youngster," he said.He added that Akhil's father worked at an electrical shop while his mother was an insurance agent."They are an ordinary family, and their future depended largely on Akhil. They had recently constructed a house," Joseph said.The family is now in touch with the local MP and MLA to seek assistance in bringing Akhil's body back to India and completing other formalities.According to foreign media reports, Ukraine's Sea Ports Authority said a cargo vessel flying the flag of Guinea-Bissau was hit by Russian forces on Sunday shortly after leaving the port of Odesa. The vessel, carrying Ukrainian corn, was reportedly struck while at sea. The authority said eight people were rescued from the ship.India strongly condemned the attack, saying that targeting commercial shipping, endangering the lives of civilian crew members, or impeding freedom of navigation and commerce is deplorable and must be avoided.

World.title: 'Bound by shared democratic values': PM Modi congratulates Andy Burnham on becoming UK Prime Minister
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday congratulated Andy Burnham on assuming office as UK PM and expressed confidence that India-UK ties would continue to deepen across key sectors.

In a post on X, PM Modi said, "Warmest congratulations to Mr Andy Burnham on assuming office as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom."

Highlighting the strong bilateral relationship, the Prime Minister said, "India and the UK are bound by shared democratic values and enjoy wide-ranging cooperation across trade, investment, technology, defence and people-to-people relations. With CETA entering into force this month, our bilateral partnership is poised to grow even stronger."

Prime Minister Modi also said he looked forward to working closely with Burnham to strengthen the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership.

"I look forward to working closely with you to further deepen the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and advance our shared Vision 2035," he added.

The UK entered another chapter of political change as the Labour Party replaced Keir Starmer following an internal leadership contest that ended his tenure as prime minister.

Andy Burnham becomes the seventh person to serve as UK prime minister in just 10 years, specifying the country's prolonged period of political churn.

World.title: Sikkim tunnel landslide: Seven dead, several feared trapped as rescue operation continues
World.content:
Ambulance and Fire tenders rush to the spot following Samardung tunnel collapse (ANI)

More details awaited...

NEW DELHI: At least seven people have died while several workers are feared trapped inside an under-construction tunnel in Sikkim's Namchi district after a landslide blocked the entrance and triggered a suspected gas leak on Monday.The incident occurred inside an under-construction tunnel at Samardung, Jholungey, in Namchi district. Authorities suspect that around 27 workers were trapped inside, although the exact number has not yet been confirmed.Rescue teams are carrying out a massive operation to evacuate those trapped, officials said."As per the latest official information, seven fatalities have been reported by the District Administration," the Namchi Information and Public Relations Department said in a statement.The bodies of the deceased have been shifted to Singtam District Hospital, STNM Hospital in Gangtok, and Namchi District Hospital, it added."There is a possibility that around 27 workers are trapped inside the tunnel. However, since complete information about the condition inside the tunnel has not yet come in, the actual number has not been confirmed," District Collector Anupa Tamling said, ANI reported."Only after the NDRF team returns will there be clear information about how many workers are inside and what their condition is," she added.The rescue operation is being carried out by the Namchi district administration, in coordination with the NDRF, State Disaster Response Force (SDRF), Sikkim Police, Fire and Emergency Services, the Health Department, and other agencies.The Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority (SSDMA) is closely monitoring the situation, and officials said further updates will be issued as more information becomes available.The incident was reported on Monday afternoon following an alleged gas leak inside the tunnel. The exact cause of the accident is yet to be ascertained.

World.title: No let-up even after strict punishment for rape: Supreme Court
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Expressing concern that there has been no let-up in incidents of rape/ gangrape despite punishment for the crimes being made stringent in the aftermath of the horrifying Nirbhaya incident, Supreme Court Monday awarded a 20-year jail term to a rickshaw puller who had raped a woman in 2016 on the pretext of taking her home from New Delhi Railway Station.

In its sentencing order, a bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih decided to take a sympathetic approach as the convict was only 25 years of age at the time of commission of offence and had no criminal antecedents. Though the trial court and Delhi High Court had sentenced him to spend the rest of his life in jail, apex court modified the quantum of sentence to a 20year jail term.

The rickshaw puller was convicted and sentenced in June 2017, and Delhi High Court upheld the order within six months in Nov.

While the convict filed an appeal after eight years, apex court decided the case within seven months. On the first date of hearing on Jan 5, apex court had made it clear that it would not interfere with the conviction order and would only examine the quantum of punishment.

The bench said that punishing an offender has a trifold purpose, i.e. punitive, deterrent and protective, and a holistic approach should be taken before deciding the quantum of punishment.





âThe overall objective is to rid society of criminal proclivity. The same is done by ensuring that the sentence imposed is proportional to the offence or, in other words, not overly influenced by the possibility of reformation and instead, striking a judicious balance between the interest of the victim, society and the accused, after following due process of law,â it said.

âIn the present case, the appellant convict has no criminal antecedents; was only 25 years old when the offence was committed; given the young age there is a possibility of reformation.

The State has neither brought on record anything to show that the same would not be possible, nor has it contravened the statement made on behalf of the appellant that in the nearly 10 years (including remission) that he has been convicted, he has maintained good conduct,â the bench said.

The court pointed out that such crimes continue to occur regularly, notwithstanding various amendments to the law to deter potential offenders. While these may have had some positive impact, the need to check such crimes with urgency cannot be understated, it said, citing NCRB data, as per which around 30,000 rape cases were reported in India in 2024.

World.title: Parliament Monsoon Session Day 2 LIVE: Both Houses adjourned till noon amid uproar; Kharge raises CJP protest crackdown in RS
World.content:
Both Houses were adjourned till noon minutes after beginning proceedings on day 2 of the Monsoon Session of Parliament on Tuesday (July 21, 2026). While Lok Sabha was adjourned with Speaker Om Birla asserting that issues will be raised post Question Hour, the Rajya Sabha broke into a din as soon as Leader of the House and Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge began speaking about the police crackdown on the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest and proposed Parliament march in New Delhi on Monday (July 20, 2026).

In a move to grant statutory protection to the National Song Vande Mataram., the Centre will likely table the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, 2026. in the Rajya Sabha on Tuesday (July 21, 2026). According to the Bill, any act causing obstruction in the singing of the National Song or insulting it in any form would become punishable under law. Meanwhile, the Lok Sabha is scheduled to take up the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026, for consideration and passing.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi chaired the NDA Parliamentary meeting in the Parliament House ahead of the day’s session.

On day 1 of the Monsoon Session, repeated adjournments disrupted Parliament’s proceedings on Monday (July 20, 2026) as Opposition protested in both Houses demanding a discussion on various issues, including the question paper leaks and the Cockroach Janta Party-led protest in Delhi’s Jantar Mantar.

Follow updates here

World.title: India summons Russian envoy over killing of four Indian seafarers near Odessa, Ukraine
World.content:
India on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) summoned the Russian charge d'affaires (CDA) and lodged a strong protest over the killing of four Indian seafarers aboard a Guinea Bissau-flagged merchant vessel off the coast of Ukraine.

The Ministry of External Affairs, in a press release on Tuesday (July 21, 2026), said that the Russian CDA Vladimir Ladanov was summoned and the Ministry conveyed to him “India’s grave concerns and unequivocal condemnation of the attack on the commercial vessel MV Golden Leo on 19 July 2026, which resulted in the tragic loss of four Indian lives”.

The Ministry said that such attacks undermine the safety, security, and stability of international maritime commerce.

“The Russian Chargé d’Affaires was requested to convey India’s strong concerns to his authorities that the targeting of commercial shipping and the resulting loss of innocent civilian lives are unacceptable and must be avoided,” the Ministry said.

Russia attacked the civilian vessel navigating Ukraine's maritime corridor on Sunday (July 19, 2026) and its crew included citizens of Syria and India. The Guinea-Bissau-flagged ship was hit by Russian cruise missiles, the Ukrainian Air Force said. The vessel— MV Golden Leo— had 17 crew members, including five Indian nationals, according to the MEA.

World.title: Tunnel collapses in Sikkim’s Namchi; 8 workers killed, rescue ops under way
World.content:
Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang on Tuesday (July 21, 2026) said eight workers were killed after an under-construction tunnel collapsed in Namchi district a day ago.

The tunnel of NHPC Teesta Stage VI Hydroelectric Project at Samardung in Jholungey caved in due to a landslide, he said.

Around 27 workers were trapped inside the under-construction tunnel after a landslide blocked its entrance and triggered a suspected gas leak on Monday afternoon, officials had said.

The rescue operation has been complicated by the presence of gas inside the tunnel, with several personnel experiencing dizziness and losing consciousness while attempting to reach the trapped workers, they said.

The gas is believed to be naturally emanating from underground strata or rock formations disturbed by the landslide, they said

The Chief Minister said Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with him and enquired about the rescue operations.

"Following the tragic incident at the under-construction tunnel of the NHPC Teesta Stage VI Hydroelectric Project at Samardung, Jholungey, in Namchi District, Hon'ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with me to enquire about the situation and the ongoing rescue operations," Mr. Tamang said on X.

He also said, "His words of concern and compassion for the affected workers and their families, along with his assurance of every possible assistance from the Government of India, have provided immense strength and reassurance to the people of Sikkim during this difficult hour."

World.title: CJP protest in Delhi LIVE: Dipke apologises to CJP supporters who were 'brutally beaten' by police

World.title: Five people dead in apparent mass drowning in Ohio river
World.content:
Two women and three men were confirmed dead on Monday (July 21, 2026) in an apparent ​mass drowning in Ohio after two people entered a river to ‌help a struggling swimmer, followed by two more ​adults who made an ill-fated rescue attempt ⁠of their own, officials said.

According to the Delaware County Sheriff’s Office, the tragedy unfolded on Sunday (July 19, 2026) night along the Scioto River at the O’Shaughnessy ‌Reservoir, about 10 miles northwest of Columbus, Ohio, the State’s capital and largest city.

A group ‌of at least seven people — two sets of ‌parents, ⁠an adult male friend, and two children — were ⁠relaxing along the river’s edge around sunset, some of them fishing, when one of the adults ventured into the river to swim, according ​to Sheriff Jeffrey Balzer.

As the ‌swimmer began to struggle in the water, two other adults tried to assist him but began floundering themselves, leading two more adults to make rescue attempts before ‌all five disappeared in the river, Mr. Balzer told ​reporters at a news conference on Monday (July 20, 2026).

“It’s not unusual, I think, for one person to ⁠be struggling in the water, and other people attempt to save him, yet they don’t have the skills to do ‌that, so we end up with multiple deaths,” the Sheriff said.

Authorities were alerted after one of the two children ran to a nearby road and flagged down a motorist, telling the driver “his family was in the river,” Mr. Balzer said.

Emergency personnel were dispatched to the ‌scene, where they quickly found two women and pulled them from the ​water. The women were pronounced dead a short time later at a local hospital, according to ⁠Balzer.

The bodies of the three missing men were recovered the ⁠next day, a spokesperson for the Sheriff’s office, Tracy Whited, later told news media outlets.

The Sheriff said ‌the two children, both under the age of 10, had since been placed in the care of ​the local family services agency.

World.title: 5,289 cyber awareness programmes held across Gujarat
World.content:
The Gujarat police has organised 5,289 cyber safety awareness programmes across the State in the first two weeks of its 28-day special campaign, Operation Surakshit Cyberspace, aimed at ensuring the safe use of online platforms by women and children.

The campaign focuses on preventing cybercrime through community engagement, technology-driven surveillance, victim outreach, cyber awareness and prompt legal action.

Additional Director General of Police (CID Crime Women Cell) Ajay Chaudhary said ensuring the online safety of women and children was a priority in the digital era. “Through Operation Surakshit Cyberspace, Gujarat Police is creating a safer digital environment by raising awareness about cyber threats such as deepfakes and sextortion. Gujarat Police remains fully committed to the safety and security of every citizen,” he said.

According to the police, 1,874 awareness and outreach programmes were organised during the first week, followed by 3,415 special sessions in the second week focusing on online threats such as sextortion, deepfakes and cyberstalking. The programmes reached lakhs of citizens across the State.

During the first week, the campaign included 185 launch events on digital and physical safety, 438 Cyber Safety Day programmes in schools, and 336 awareness activities under Kishori Diwas for adolescent girls. The police also conducted 318 programmes for parents, 281 training sessions for teachers, 207 awareness programmes in colleges and organised 109 cyber safety rallies across districts.

In the second week, Gujarat Police organised 4,172 thematic programmes and public awareness camps. These included 743 programmes on social media safety, 578 deepfake awareness sessions, 514 cyberstalking prevention programmes and 520 events under Anti-Sextortion Day.

The police also conducted 512 gaming safety programmes, 466 online grooming prevention sessions and 461 public awareness camps in remote areas.

As part of the campaign, responsibilities have been assigned to field officers ranging from police constables and head constables to assistant sub-inspectors, police sub-inspectors and police inspectors. Their performance is being assessed on five parameters: awareness, prevention, enforcement, quality of investigation and public trust.

They appealed to citizens to report cybercrime or online harassment immediately by calling the National Cyber Helpline at 1930 and registering a complaint.

World.title: Andy Burnham becomes U.K. PM, promising new social and political model
World.content:
Former Manchester Mayor, Andrew Burnham, was appointed Prime Minister of the U.K. on Monday (July 20, 2026), its seventh in a decade. Mr. Burnham described the moment as a “circuit breaker”, as he promised to usher in a new political and social model for the country, taking power out of London and spreading it across the regions of the U.K.

The outgoing Prime Minister Keir Starmer, who had made history two years ago, when he led the Labour Party in one of the largest victories in modern times, made history again on Monday (July 20, 2026), but this time for becoming the U.K.’s shortest serving Labour Prime Minister

“I go with good grace, I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved,” Mr. Starmer said in brief remarks outside on Downing Street, as he wished his successor “every success”.

Editorial | Downing streak: On the Starmer resignation, British politics

“We will make this moment a circuit breaker for Britain, bringing forward the biggest changes in the last 40 years: a new political model and a new economic model,” Mr. Burnham said outside No.10 Downing Street, minutes after he was ceremonially invited to form a government by Britain’s Monarch King Charles III. Mr Burnham’s wife, the Dutch-born Marie-France van Heel, was also present as were large numbers of the Prime Minister’s supporters, including his mother and Josh Simons, the MP who vacated his Makerfield seat, so Mr Burnham could win it and return to Westminster.

“I am acutely conscious that I am … the seventh Prime Minister since 2016, making this a moment for reflection and new resolution,” Mr. Burnham said, adding that Britain needed to show the world it could regain its stability. He went on to add that the U.K. had taken wrong turns since the 1980s, by privatizing economic power and centralizing political power.

Andy Burnham: U.K.’s latest PM | Infographics

He reiterated his messages from recent months including his wish to see greater greater public control of utilities, supporting supporting young people to enter and stay in the workforce to bring down the welfare bill and spreading power more evenly across the U.K.

“…We will take power out of here and carry it into every postcode in the land,” he said. Mr Burnham had said in recent weeks that he would create a ‘No. 10 North’ — a hub office in Manchester to manage the redistribution of power. His first actions in office on Monday would be to “end rough sleeping [homelessness]” in the U.K., Mr. Burnham said.

The U.K. would have a new ten year plan, later this year, Mr. Burnham said, adding that he would issue more immediate orders starting Tuesday, to help with the cost of living along with details on how he would fund this. His first action in office on Monday would be to “end rough sleeping [homelessness]” in the U.K.

Mr Burnham did not mention Mr. Starmer’s name during his remarks, although he paid tribute to the man he ousted, on Friday, after accepting the leadership of their party. Mr. Burnham has had longstanding leadership ambitions; he tried unsuccessfully to become party Leader in 2010 and 2015.

The new Prime Minister has used the word ‘Manchesterism’ to describe his policies – which included the unification of Manchester’s public transport networks under greater public oversight. Little, however, is known about Mr. Burnham’s foreign policy generally and regarding the U.K.-India relationship.

The 56-year-old Mr, Burnham is pro-European; he has said previously that he hopes to see the U.K. back in the E.U. during his lifetime although he said he would not act to bring that about during his term in office. He apologized in recent days for Labour’s initial position on the Israel-Gaza conflict and has promised firmer actions against Israel. He appears to be pro-NATO and has indicated he will be bound by Mr. Starmer’s £15 billion defence investment plan which was announced in recent days. Mr. Burhnam recently said that British support for Ukraine “will not waiver” and that the U.S. was the county’s most important security ally. The new Prime Minister has committed to keeping Jonathan Powell in post as the U.K.’s national security adviser.

Keir Starmer resigns

Roughly an hour and a half before Mr Burnham’s speech, Mr Starmer had spoken outside No. 10, surrounded by his wife Victoria, supporters and members of his administration — including outgoing Chancellor of the Exchequer Rachel Reeves, Deputy Prime Minister David Lammy and London’s mayor Sadiq Khan.

Mr. Starmer, a centrist, struggled to hold Labour together since 2024, with internecine battles growing over policy differences ranging from welfare spending to Labour not taking a strong enough stance against Israel for its killing of civilians in Gaza.

Mr. Starmer’s credibility within the party took a further hit around his appointment of a controversial U.S. envoy and the resignation of several of his key staffers. His relationship with union leaders began to sour when he was still Leader of the Opposition, after he sacked an MP who had made an unauthorised media appearance alongside rail workers on a picket line. These ties frayed further despite his government passing the Employment Rights Acts 2025 to strengthen certain rights for workers. For instance, Labour lost support among energy workers over net-zero policies.

Reports of his managerial style within the party and the Cabinet also cost Mr. Starmer support from his colleagues. The final blows to Mr Starmer’s position came after Labour lost a crucial byelection to the Greens in the north west of England this year, followed by a major defeat to Reform in English council elections and losses to other parties in the Welsh and Scottish Assembly elections in May.

Mr. Starmer was given an emotional farewell during the weekly parliamentary Prime Minister’s Questions (PMQs) last week, with colleagues and Opposition leaders praising him. In speeches, social media posts and interviews, Mr. Starmer and some of his colleagues — including Mr. Burnham — have sought in recent days to clearly articulate the outgoing Prime Minister’s achievements as a means to give Mr. Starmer’s exit dignity and order.

The message has included Mr. Starmer being responsible for Labour’s return from the political wilderness in 2024, actions to tackle child poverty in the U.K. such as the two-child benefit cap, strengthening workers’ and tenants’ rights, cutting wait times for medical appointments in the public healthcare system, and his support for Ukraine.

Watch | U.K. PM Keir Starmer resigns: What went wrong?

In his farewell address, Mr. Starmer said Britain’s reputation on the world stage had “been greatly enhanced”.

“We face a world now where our enemies will stop at nothing to divide us, because of our values, our freedom, our decency, and frankly, because of our unflinching resolve towards the brave people of Ukraine,” Mr. Starmer said, without naming Russia.

The outgoing Prime Minister had visited both Kyiv and Paris during his last week in office, receiving one of France’s highest national awards, the Légion d’Honneur, from French President Emmanuel Macron for his work in working with France to enhance European security. Mr. Starmer had launched a “reset” of the U.K.’s relations with the European Union following the country’s exit from the bloc under the Conservatives in 2016. Last week, a trade deal with India — talks for which began under the Conservatives — came into force. Mr. Starmer had vowed a “reset” of ties with India and the Indian government in 2023, in the face of tensions due to Labour’s earlier position on Kashmir and fraying support for Labour among Indian Britons.

As he returned to the backbenches, Mr. Starmer had fought to stay on in post — including by opposing Mr. Burnham’s attempts to contest a byelection in February. However, when a colleague vacated the Makerfield parliamentary seat so Mr. Burnham could contest it, Labour’s leadership team, including Mr. Starmer were compelled to permit it. Mr. Burnham won that election on June 18 and returned to Westminster.

At PMQs last week, Mr Starmer said he “wholeheartedly” supported his successor. Asked what advice he would give the incoming Prime Minister, Mr. Starmer had said that he would provide counsel “privately, when asked, not publicly, when not asked”.

World.title: Indian man jailed in Singapore for Rs 1.49 crore diamond heist
World.content:
An Indian national has been jailed in Singapore for stealing a diamond worth around SGD200,000 (USD 154,000, roughly Rs 1.49 crore), from a China Town jewellery store. His alleged accomplice has been convicted and the sentence will be out on Friday, news agency PTI reported.

Mangroliya Manojkumar Kurjibhai, 41, was handed a jail term of two years, two months and two weeks on Friday, 17 July, after pleading guilty to one count of theft. The case against his alleged partner, Serasiya Milan Ramnikbhai, 30, has been listed for hearing on Friday.



How the swap unfolded

One man distracted a shop assistant while the other swapped a genuine 4.95-carat diamond for a counterfeit, concealing the real stone in his mouth. The pair had planned to substitute the gem before flying out of Singapore, but were caught before they could leave via Changi Airport.

Also read Indian national gets six months’ jail for molesting Singapore Airlines crew member

Both men, who met through a mutual acquaintance, had travelled to Singapore on social visit passes, PTI reported. Before arriving, they had reportedly commissioned a fake diamond in Surat, crafted to match the targeted stone’s specifications and serial number though court documents did not detail how they had obtained this information beforehand, according to the Monday report.

The heist at Dianoche

The two entered Singapore through Changi Airport on 19 June 2026, intending to steal the 4.95-carat diamond from a jewellery store, ‘Dianoche’, in China Town. They walked into the store around 3 PM and asked to see the gem.



Mangroliya kept the sales manager occupied by asking to see other items in the shop, giving Milan the opportunity to carry out the swap spitting out the fake stone and replacing it with the genuine one, which he then hid in his mouth. The act was caught on the store’s CCTV cameras, PTI said.

Mangroliya reportedly told the manager the pair would think over the purchase before leaving. Once they had gone, the manager tested the stone with an optical gemstone identification device and discovered it was a fake.

Arrest at Changi Airport

The two men returned to their hotel, checked out earlier than planned and booked an evening flight back to India, PTI reported. They were arrested at around 8.50 PM at Changi Airport’s Terminal 3 while going through immigration, and the genuine diamond was recovered from Milan’s bag.

Mangroliya was charged on June 20 and has remained in police custody since. Prosecutors left sentencing to the court’s discretion, though State Prosecuting Officer Yip Cheng Yee flagged several aggravating factors, including that the pair had entered Singapore specifically to carry out the offence. PTI quoted Yip as telling the court, “The offence was premeditated and involved a degree of planning.”

If you are enjoying this post, will you share it with someone else who might, too?



In mitigation, Mangroliya, speaking through an interpreter, said he had two children in India and asked for a lighter sentence, PTI reported. The offence of theft in a building carries a maximum penalty of seven years’ imprisonment and a fine.

World.title: Mumbai rains weather forecast: Heavy rains to intensify, warns IMD; orange alert to continue as monsoon revives
World.content:
As Mumbai continues to receive moderate rainfall for the second consecutive day, amidst the revival of monsoon currents, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) upgraded its weather warning for the city, predicting intense showers starting Tuesday, July 21, onwards. The IMD has also sounded an orange alert which will continue in Mumbai and its neighbouring districts of Thane and Raigad until Wednesday, July 22, morning.

In Mumbai, Thane and Raigad, the rain condition is expected to remain disruptive with an orange alert in place until Wednesday morning. However, heavy showers may still continue in Mumbai, Thane and Raigad until coming Saturday since the IMD has issued a yellow alert for the regions.

From Tuesday, July 21, the showers are expected to intensify further, with the possibility of heavy to very heavy rainfall coupled with gusty winds at the speed of 50 to 60 kmph, meteorologists have indicated.

Monsoon revives in Mumbai

On Tuesday, Mumbai woke up to an overcast sky and steady spells of rain across the city. The suburban pockets have received an average of 45 mm rainfall between Monday and Tuesday morning.

Records from the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation’s (BMC) weather stations showed that between Monday and Tuesday morning, the eastern suburbs recorded the heaviest spells at an average of 45.04 mm rain, followed by 36 mm rain in the island city division and 28.40 mm rain in the western suburbs.



According to the IMD, the suburban station at Santacruz received 48 mm rain during the same period while the Colaba coastal observatory recorded 35 mm rainfall.

Like Mumbai, its neighbouring region of Navi Mumbai also experienced continuous spells of rainfall with 92 mm rainfall recorded in Belapur, 85.40 mm rain in Nerul, 69 mm in Vashi and 51 mm rain in Airoli.

With rainfall gaining pace in the past few days, the lake levels recorded a continuous uptick with the total stock in the seven lakes. On Tuesday morning, the water stock touched 58 percent or 8.35 lakh million litres. Over the past 24 hours, significant rainfall was recorded over the catchment areas with 100 mm rain recorded over Bhatsa lake, 105 mm rain recorded over Tansa and 96 mm rain over Upper Vaitarna.



This marks the comeback of the monsoon rain after a prolonged hiatus of nearly two weeks. Earlier in the first week of July, incessant showers had swept across the region with over 1,000 mm rainfall recorded in seven days in Mumbai.

As the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)’s protest march in Delhi continues to dominate social media, stories of people extending support in their own ways are also grabbing attention online.

World.title: Haryana drafts Right to Business Bill, proposes 3-year inspection-free period for MSMEs
World.content:
The proposed Haryana Right to Business Bill, 2026 will grant eligible MSMEs self-declaration approvals and a three-year exemption from routine inspections. (X/Nayab Singh Saini)

The Haryana government has proposed a new law to make it easier for eligible manufacturing Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) to start businesses. Under the proposed Haryana Right to Business Bill, 2026, eligible MSMEs will receive an In-Principle Approval Certificate based on self-declaration and will not face routine government inspections for the first three years.

The Bill also proposes a two-tier approval system to provide faster clearances through a single-window mechanism. The Haryana Enterprises Promotion Centre (HEPC) will act as the State Nodal Agency, while District Level Clearance Committees will handle approvals at the district level.

The Haryana Department of Industries and Commerce drafted the Bill. This was informed during a high-level review meeting chaired by Chief Secretary Anurag Rastogi on Monday.

World.title: How Rodri won the Golden Ball with no goal, no assist, no defining stat
World.content:
Rodri and America. It was always meant to be; a unique relationship forged by chance and moulded by destiny. Sixteen years before he kissed the World Cup trophy, confetti showering on him and fireworks wiggling into East Rutherford skies, he was in Connecticut, almost 100 miles from the scene of his conquest, as part of an exchange programme.

His father wanted him to pursue academics in the United States, but he was firm on his ultimate desire to be a footballer. But his father had other plans, and imagining that the American life would alter his son’s ambitions, he packed him off to a student programme in Connecticut. Rodri. Suddenly, the quiet teenager from the Madrid suburb of Villanueva de la Cañada found himself in the middle of a forest in Conn-et-ee-cut, as they call it. “It was like I was stepping into a Hollywood movie,” he wrote in Player’s Tribune. “You know the movies where the kids go to the camp on a big lake and there’s wooden canoes and you’re climbing trees and sleeping in tents and starting fires with sticks?” Everything felt strange for the true blue Madrid boy.



ALSO READ | Spain didn’t just win the World Cup. They made an argument for greatness

One day, he called his friends to play football. They thought it was American football. “No, no that’s not what I meant, soccer,” he told them. “Oh, saw-ker. No buddy, no way,” they said. He had a football with him and played all alone. Days, nights, in the peak of summer, in the dead of winter. He didn’t mind football’s improvised version, but he remained, at heart, a dissident loyal to the footie. “Genuine fun! I kind of liked it,” he wrote.

He didn’t miss home, swiftly learned English, with a typical Connecticut accent that endeared him to his friends. It would be the same quick grasping skills that made him indispensable in the teams of two antithetical managers, Diego Simeone and Pep Guardiola, the angel and the archangel. But he began to miss home when the World Cup began. “I couldn’t even check the internet, so I was in pain,” he said.



But the main office had a clunky computer. Every day, he asked the counselors for the score. One of them told him that Spain lost to Switzerland in the first round. His heart sank. “I thought they were pulling a prank.” By the knockouts, the counsellors would tell him without asking whether Spain won or not. He was on a canoeing trip when Spain beat Germany in the semifinal. “I never felt so far from home, but also close to home, if you understand what I mean,” he would say. He pleaded with the counsellor to let him watch the final on the computer. He did, but the internet was wobbly and he had to find an illegal stream. “When Iniesta scored, I literally started screaming and I ran outside and sprinted around the lake. The guys thought I was crazy.”



Rodri poses with the Golden Ball award at the end of the World Cup final. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis) Rodri poses with the Golden Ball award at the end of the World Cup final. (AP Photo/Ashley Landis)

Sixteen years later, his friends would have realised the essence of his scream. He was holding the most precious trophy in the world aloft. A dream beyond for a Madrid boy.

***

The route from Connecticut to New Jersey took years in the making. A year later, he returned home, and to his father’s anguish his son was still in love with the game. He let him be. “It was almost like a drug,” he once said. He journeyed from Atletico Madrid’s academy to Villarreal’s, before returning to Atletico as a senior player. The first big influence in his career was waiting for him, the manager Simeone. The Argentine sensed that he has marvellous technical finesse but not the nastiness his teams embodied.



“When I was at Villarreal, I was very good with the ball at my feet, but I was still a bit soft. With Diego Simeone, I learned what it means to be the bad guy – to be a bit of a b****** on the pitch. It was about making the other team a mess for 90 minutes. That was another important piece.” Simeone realised that he could be a bad guy without resorting to tactical fouls, without the opponents realising his meanness.

Rodri’s positional sense is so supreme that he is never out of his place to commit a nasty foul. A defensive fielder has the image of a tackle-happy, tough mean guy. But the finest of them are not, from the irrepressible Claude Makelele and Sergio Busquets to N’Golo Kante and Rodri. They have more time and space than all, a preternatural sense of the ball, the paths it would travel. This World Cup, he was ranked 97th in the list of offenders. That’s the paradox of Rodri, he won the golden ball without a single goal or assist, without topping any of the defensive or attacking metrics. Even in pass completion rate, he sits 44th on the table. So what made him the tournament’s most valuable player?



His second, and perhaps most influential, figure in life was Guardiola, who would say: “The way he sees the game, no one else sees, to its finest details, his vision is panoramic.”

Rodri made Messi play increasingly with the right foot, lethal but not as much as his left peg. (AP Photo/Julio Cortez) Rodri made Messi play increasingly with the right foot, lethal but not as much as his left peg. (AP Photo/Julio Cortez)

When he arrived in City, he was far from the midfield figurehead he is now. Guardiola advised: “Don’t move too much, a holding midfielder does not, move just enough and only when it is required.” Guardiola was surprised how fast he learned, and adapted. He enhanced his passing range, polished his positional awareness, and began his ascent to greatness.



ALSO READ | Sun sets on World Cup football’s greatest career as Messi tears drown out final

In a year, he became irreplaceable for City. Their fortunes have hinged directly on his availability and optimal fitness. “People always look at the players who score goals, but football is much more than that. Rodri controlled every match he played. He dictated the tempo, protected the defence, recovered possession, started attacks and gave every player around him the confidence to play their football,” Guardiola praised him.

In the final, he tied up Messi in knots, so much so that he began avoiding him like a thief would a policeman. Rodri made him play increasingly with the right foot, lethal but not as much as his left peg. Messi would have found traces of his old friend Sergio Busquets. Like the Barcelona cornerstone, he can’t be judged with stats, cannot be defined with his nomenclatural role. To label him as a defensive midfielder would be turning a blind eye to his attacking output, to call him a tempo-setter is an inaccurate compartmentalisation. He is, as Luis de la Fuente calls him, the traffic controller, whose role is not as glamorous as the secret agents or the sleuths, but controls the immediate world around him. He is the axis of the compass that lets Spain draw a perfect circle, a man whose occupancy of vital spaces sucks half the belief of his opponents. Argentina would readily vouch for the invisible man that made them anonymous.



He perhaps exists in a state of paradox, a tempo-setter who is a holding midfielder, a disciple of both Simeone and Guardiola, a conductor who is also the lead vocals, and a true blue Madrid boy speaking “Conn-et-ee-cut” English. Also, the best midfielder in the world, a player whose numbers can’t capture him, and whose role defies definition.

World.title: Diljit Dosanjh supports CJP protest: ‘Students shouldn’t have been treated this way’
World.content:
Actor-singer Diljit Dosanjh has backed students participating in the protests launched by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). Dosanjh took to social media on Tuesday morning and shared a note requesting the authorities to listen to the students’ demands. He also acknowledged that he might be tagged as an ‘anti-national’ for supporting the students, and said that he faced a lot of backlash, as well as legal troubles, when he previously spoke in favour of farmers’ protest in 2020.

Diljit’s note, which was partially written in Punjabi, can be translated as, “What happened today was really sad… Students shouldn’t have been treated this way. I request the authorities to listen to the demands of the students. The voice of the masses is the voice of god.” He further wrote, “I have been tagged as an anti-nationalist on many occasions. Even now, I will be called an anti-nationalist. After the farmers’ protest, I faced a lot of backlash and legal problems which I can’t even discuss. Rest, god is watching everything. May god bless.”

In December 2020, Diljit Dosanjh joined the farmers protesting at Delhi’s Singhu border. Following this, the actor-singer recived a lot of backlash from those who did not support the protestors.

Diljit Dosanjh expresses solidarity with the students. (Photo: Diljit Dosanjh/Instagram) Diljit Dosanjh expresses solidarity with the students. (Photo: Diljit Dosanjh/Instagram)

Vir Das, Huma Qureshi, Anurag Kashyap support students’ protest

Besides Diljjit Dosanjh, Vir Das also expressed his solidarity for the students via social media. “If you’re an Indian live artist. I hope you understand the sheer hypocrisy of not speaking up for young people, and then trying to sell them tickets later. The sheer luxury of being a silent viewer to what an Indian crowd cares about, and then expecting an Indian crowd to be loud and vocal and care about you. Apna apna dekh lo, lekin mere liye pahunch jaana. Doesn’t work,” he wrote.

Anurag Kashyap questioned the actions of the police personnel present at the protests and wondered if they could raise their voice against the orders they were being handed down.

Actor Riteish Deshmukh also expressed solidarity with the students by sharing a joint statement with wife, actor Genelia Deshmukh. “We stand in solidarity with the youth of our country. Their voices deserve to be heard, loud, clear, and without fear. They are the heartbeat of our democracy and the true architects of our nation’s future. Let us listen, support, and empower them. The energy, courage, and dreams of our young people will shape the India we aspire to build.” Huma Qureshi also shared her support for the protesting students and wrote on social media, “Seeing peaceful protesters being met with such brute force and lathis left me with a deep sense of sadness. This surely could have been handled with more patience, more listening, and more dialogue.”

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Shabana Azmi (@azmishabana18)

Shabana Azmi at CJP protest

Venran actors Shabana Azmi and Prakash Raj were also present at the protests at Jantar Mantar and shared videos from the site. In a chat with India Today, Azmi insisted that students were demonstrating in a non-violent way but the authorities tried to blame them for initing lathicharge. “I was right there when the tear gassing happened and I was witness to the children being lathi-charged, and also girls… young girls being lathi-charged. They tried to put the blame on the students and said somebody threw a shoe and that’s how they started, but that’s not what I saw and that’s not what all the students kept saying. They were showing me their wounds and they were saying they wanted to do a completely non-violent protest, which is what was being told to them constantly from the podium,” she said.

World.title: Kerala Board Plus Two SAY exam 2026 results likely this week
World.content:
The Directorate of Higher Secondary Education (DHSE), Kerala, is expected to announce the Save A Year (SAY) Plus Two examination results soon on its official websites — pareekshabhavan.kerala.gov.in, prd.kerala.gov.in, results.kite.kerala.gov.in and keralaresults.nic.in.
